segments.teaches: a machine is a depreciating asset: its value falls every year until it is worthless; the government sets depreciation rates

heading 'machine' with a red tag of the yearly depreciation percentage added later
red bracketed label: depreciating asset
blue chips gross produce / net produce on the right

segments.notes: The decay curve draws itself in two stages (short arrow, then extended to zero). National emblem should not be reused.
segments.idea: a machine is a depreciating asset: it loses value every year until it is worth nothing; the government sets the rates

segments.example: machine worth 1 crore falls to zero over 20 years

segments.teaches: depreciation is booked as an expense; value falls from 1 crore to 70 lakh, a 30 lakh expense that can wipe out a 25 lakh profit, so no tax

elements.what: blue two-row year/value table: start year 1 crore, next year 70 lakh (new value in red)
dotted curved arrow from the table to a pink depreciation (expense) card showing 30 lakh
green year/profit card showing 25 lakh, placed beside the expense card
thick grey frame grouping profit and expense
arrow from the frame to a bold 'no tax' label

segments.notes: Running numeric example continues (1 crore -> 70 lakh -> 30 lakh expense vs 25 lakh profit). The graph is swapped for the number table in the same slot.
segments.idea: depreciation is an expense: 1 crore -> 70 lakh is a 30 lakh expense, which can wipe out a 25 lakh profit, so no tax
segments.shown_as: the graph is swapped for a year/value table (1 crore, then 70 lakh in red); a dotted arrow carries the drop to a pink 30 lakh expense card set beside a green 25 lakh profit card; a grey frame groups them and an arrow points to a bold 'no tax'
segments.example: 1 crore -> 70 lakh = 30 lakh expense vs 25 lakh profit -> no tax

segments.teaches: the machine makes 10 lakh bottles at 10 each: gross produce 1 crore, net produce 1 crore minus 30 lakh depreciation

elements.what: pink depreciation card moved up under the machine

segments.idea: 10 lakh bottles at 10 each make gross produce 1 crore; net produce is 1 crore minus 30 lakh depreciation

segments.teaches: GDP minus depreciation = NDP; GNP minus depreciation = NNP; depreciation counts only assets used for production

segments.notes: Equations are aligned so the common term forms one highlighted column. Everyday-object example (phone) for the business-use rule.
segments.idea: GDP - depreciation = NDP and GNP - depreciation = NNP; only assets used for production count
segments.shown_as: two stacked equations share one cream depreciation column in red; a pointer box above says only assets used to produce count, with a phone labelled 'used for business' as the example
